label: verify-bm-natural-benchmarks

claims.claim: Natural pine-cone bilayers give m^2 n = 2 to 5.7, f = 1.23-1.46 (82-97% of 3/2 ceiling); Reyssat m~1,n~5 gives 83%; paper strip 98.8%
claims.source_says: decreased upon water uptake linearly from ESF,30% = 800 MPa to ESF,75% = 200 MPa ... sclereid layer ... from ESC,50% = 35 MPa to ESC,60% = 25 MPa ... sclerenchyma fiber strands ... around 500 µm
claims.note: Source supports the moduli and ~500 um fibre thickness, but the m^2n, f and percent-of-ceiling values are the agent's own arithmetic (and Reyssat and the paper strip are not in this source); the 1000 um sclereid thickness was not found.

claims.claim: Pine-cone benchmarks: active ~1 mm, passive ~0.5 mm; 21% differential strain (22% vs 1%); ~11% over 0-100 %RH; 29 min wet / 96 min dry; 4.5 wt% at 80 %RH
claims.source_says: In the wet state, the sclereid layer was 27% thicker and 22% longer in the bending zone ... fiber strands ... 1% longer. The sclereid cells (93 mg, 23 °C, 80% rh) absorbed 4.5 wt%
claims.note: 22%, 1% and 4.5 wt% at 80% rh are confirmed and 11% contraction is for 80 to 30% rh, not 0-100; the 29/96 min times and 1 mm active thickness were not found.

claims.claim: Timoshenko-type theory fits pine cone only fairly well and over-predicts unless ~50% lower wet moduli are used
claims.source_says: A fairly good agreement is obtained ... even if overestimation is observed ... we need to take into account a 50% reduction of Young's modulus for dry tissue to fit the experimental data with the model
claims.note: Matches PMC4733047; the 800 to 200 MPa link is from the other paper and is the agent's inference.

claims.claim: Flytrap closes in ~100 ms by snap-buckling; Erodium coil from single tilted cellulose layer (20 to 10 degrees); ceiling applies only to pine cone, sesame, paper strip
claims.source_says: The rapid closure of the Venus flytrap (Dionaea muscipula) leaf in about 100 ms ... the fast closure of the trap results from a snap-buckling instability
claims.note: Flytrap 100 ms and snap-buckling confirmed; the PubMed record says nothing on water transport taking minutes, Erodium, or the scope judgment.

overall: Core numbers (moduli, 22% vs 1%, 4.5 wt%, 500 um, 100 ms snap-buckling, 50% modulus reduction) check out. The m^2n/f/percent-of-ceiling values are the agent's derived arithmetic. The 29/96 min response times, the 1 mm active-layer thickness, Erodium, and flytrap water-transport timing are not in the cited sources.
